import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a comprehensive figure with multiple subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Specifications Analysis (1000 Cameras)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# 1. Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type (scatter plot)
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_types = df['sensor_type'].unique()
colors = sns.color_palette('husl', n_colors=len(sensor_types))
for sensor, color in zip(sensor_types, colors):
    data = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(data['megapixels'], data['price_usd'], alpha=0.6, 
                label=sensor, s=50, color=color)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Camera Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', fontsize=9)
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Average price by brand (top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
brand_stats = df.groupby('brand').agg({'price_usd': 'mean', 'brand': 'count'}).rename(columns={'brand': 'count'})
top_brands = brand_stats.nlargest(10, 'count')
brands_sorted = top_brands.sort_values('price_usd', ascending=True)
bars = ax2.barh(brands_sorted.index, brands_sorted['price_usd'], color=sns.color_palette('viridis', len(brands_sorted)))
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Average Camera Price by Top 10 Brands', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)
# Add value labels
for i, (idx, val) in enumerate(brands_sorted['price_usd'].items()):
    ax2.text(val, i, f' ${val:.0f}', va='center', fontsize=9)

# 3. Distribution of cameras over model years with 4K capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
year_4k = df.groupby('model_year')['has_video_4k'].agg(['sum', 'count'])
year_4k['no_4k'] = year_4k['count'] - year_4k['sum']
x_years = year_4k.index
width = 0.8
ax3.bar(x_years, year_4k['sum'], width, label='4K Video', color='#2ecc71', alpha=0.8)
ax3.bar(x_years, year_4k['no_4k'], width, bottom=year_4k['sum'], label='No 4K Video', color='#e74c3c', alpha=0.8)
ax3.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_title('Camera Count by Year and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(fontsize=10)
ax3.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 4. Weight vs Max ISO colored by body type
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
colors_body = sns.color_palette('Set2', n_colors=len(body_types))
for body, color in zip(body_types, colors_body):
    data = df[df['body_type'] == body]
    ax4.scatter(data['weight_grams'], data['max_iso'], alpha=0.6, 
                label=body, s=50, color=color)
ax4.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_ylabel('Max ISO', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_title('Camera Weight vs Max ISO by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='Body Type', fontsize=9)
ax4.set_yscale('log')
ax4.grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
